changed_views: Open-weight models can function as an exit option that supports adoption of closed American systems, complicating a simple substitution framing.

signals.claim: Tyler Cowen argues that attempts to ban or sanction Chinese open-weight models will be ineffective.
signals.evidence: He points to multinational affiliates, existing use by major US companies, and eventual on-device deployment as practical enforcement barriers.

signals.claim: Cowen argues that Chinese open-weight models can complement rather than merely displace American AI systems.
signals.evidence: He says a credible open-source fallback makes customers more willing to adopt US platforms because they retain an exit option if access changes.

signals.claim: Cowen forecasts that AI-native young founders will create high-revenue companies with very small teams across knowledge industries.
signals.evidence: He describes teenagers already mastering AI and building companies, and expects similar founders to compete in medicine, law, consulting, and banking where regulation permits.

signals.claim: Cowen says current youth-employment data do not support the claim that capable language models have already destroyed the entry-level labor market.
signals.evidence: He cites the unemployment rate for people aged eighteen to twenty-four as having returned to its pre-capable-LLM level, while noting that the broader labor market has slowed.
